note: What each database actually holds for the parishes this archive needs. Checked before searching, every time — because a search of a source that does not cover your parish returns nothing, and nothing looks exactly like a negative result.

rows.note: Countess of Huntingdon's Chapel, Methodist Bishopston, Moravian Maudlin Street, Temple of Holy Cross. St Paul — the parish this archive needs — is not among them.
Stops 128 years before Hannah Saniger was born. Her baptism is untranscribed, not missing.
Covers the whole Saniger chain. This is where the chain was tested and failed.
With Dursley, holds 340 of the 494 Saniger records in the county.
Tested as the alternative reading of the tree's “Berkley”. The family there is SINGER throughout and holds no Hannah near 1805.

rows.holds: one D'Arcy record in the whole county
rows.note: That one record is Joseph D'Arcy's baptism, 19 March 1780, naming Robert and Jean. The 1779 marriage itself is not in the transcription.
Holds both the 1742 baptism that killed the Keele graft and the 1744 burial that may undo it.

128 Murdoch records exist for Ayrshire — Galston, Tarbolton, Ayr, Kirkoswald, Loudoun, Dailly, Beith, Dunlop — and not one for St Quivox. The county itself is thin: 202 Smiths for the whole eighteenth century.
Midlothian's holding is Edinburgh, Canongate, Restalrig and Dalry. Jean Ward's birth parish is not transcribed.
Zero records for the entire county. A control search for SMITH across the eighteenth century returns nothing. The county is offered in the search form and has no data behind it.
HO107/374 — this is where James and Hannah Wakefield were found, with Miriam aged one.

rows.holds: 221 Gloucestershire Wakefields, 31 in Bristol — but not this family
rows.note: Nationally only 36% of the 1851 pieces are transcribed. The piece covering Drivers Fields is not among them — which is why the Lyddya Sinegar identification is still an inference.
Control-tested at 21,248 Wakefield marriages for 1838–1842 before any absence was reported from it. This is where Miriam's birth registration was found.

rows.where: Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills, England
rows.holds: a wills index 1750–1800 and an administrations index 1660–1700
rows.note: NOTHING AFTER 1800. Three wills this archive needs — Robert D'Arcy's of 1827, Joseph D'Arcy's of 1848 and John Maddock Jones's of 1844 — are all beyond it. A paid trial does not help; the records are not there to unlock.

rows.where: Gloucestershire probate, Consistory Court of Gloucester
rows.note: Covers Berkeley and the whole Vale in the right years. Searched under wildcards for every form of the Saniger name and returns two entries, neither of them at Berkeley. A real negative, control-tested at 277 Smiths.

rows.where: Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage Licence Bonds, DUBLIN diocese
rows.note: Sorted by year, the latest Dublin-diocese entries in the entire set are a single 1813, a single 1752, and then a wall of 1741. The catalogue date range is the set's range, not the diocese's. An 1819 Wicklow marriage cannot be in it.

rows.where: Betham Prerogative Marriage Licences Abstracts, Ireland
rows.note: Ends nine years before the marriage this archive wants. Twenty-two Darcy entries, all necessarily too early.

rows.where: British consular and overseas registers (deaths abroad)
rows.note: Searched the whole record-set catalogue for “consular” and for “abroad” and both return no record sets at all. The Le Havre deaths of 1843 are not reachable here; they are on Ancestry and at Kew in RG 35.

rows.where: Caribbean Birth & Baptism Index — St Michael, Barbados
rows.note: Holds the two christenings of Robert D'Arcy's children at St Michael in 1786 and 1788. Barbados Births & Baptisms 1637-1891, a separate and larger set, holds neither — two indexes of the same island disagreeing about what is in them, which is its own warning.

The index is searchable on a paid trial and the transcripts are not — “Subscribe to unlock exclusive records”. Joseph D'Arcy's whole artillery career and a Constantine D'Arcy entry of 1777-79 are visible as dates and unreadable as records.

rows.where: any census set, when a YEAR OF BIRTH and a PLACE are combined
rows.note: A query carrying both yearofbirth and keywordsplace returns ZERO on census sets and presents it as a clean negative. Control: JANE SMITH born about 1788 in Sussex, 1871 — zero. The same search returns 60 by year alone and 136 by place alone. Search on one or the other and filter by hand.

rows.where: a NAMED CEMETERY — Centenary Memorial Gardens, Brisbane
rows.note: Searching inside a named cemetery works and produced three D'Arcy memorials with plots and dates. This archive had never used the source.

rows.where: by SURNAME AND STATE — location=Queensland, locationId=state_2118
rows.note: Returns NO MATCHES for D'Arcy, Darcy, Sneyd — and for SMITH, which is impossible, while Darcy worldwide returns 10,654. The locationId is wrong. Search within a cemetery instead.

The site loads and its own search API then answers 403 and 400; the country list never finishes loading and the page sits on “Please wait”. Nothing was searched, so nothing is known — this is a blocked source and not an empty one.

rows.where: ARIENZO, Caserta — the parish this family married into
rows.holds: 422 REGISTERS: Matrimoni processetti 63, Matrimoni 62, Nati 59, Morti 57, Diversi 45, and more
rows.note: Digitised in full and free to read — AND NOT NAME-INDEXED. A search for FALCO at Arienzo returns nothing, and so does a search for RUSSO, the commonest surname in Campania, which is the control that proves the index rather than the family is missing. Antenati says so itself: only part of its registers are indexed. These 422 must be read page by page. The marriage PROCESSETTI are the prize, because they carry birth extracts and parental consents for both parties.

rows.db: National Library of Ireland parish registers
rows.where: the Limerick line — Atkinson, Cole, Creech, Kent, Bowen, Peevers
rows.note: The NLI collection is Catholic by definition, and this line is not. Paul Cole Atkinson is recorded as born at ST MARY'S, LIMERICK — the Church of Ireland cathedral parish — and the surnames around him are Protestant settler names. The same shape as the Wicklow problem: the right records are the ones the NLI does not hold.

rows.where: the Creech, Atkinson and Mulcahy lines
rows.note: A Cloudflare bot check, for the third time in this archive's life. Not defeated, and will not be. The free official Irish index remains unreachable from here and stays on the errand list for a person with a browser.
Reachable, and behind Login / Register / Subscribe. Limerick and both Tipperarys are among its counties. It is a subscription, so it is an errand and not a search.

The old-parish-register search area answers ACCESS DENIED without an account. No account was created and no credentials were entered. Jean Ward's 1754 baptism and her parents' 1747 marriage are already held here from FamilySearch; what ScotlandsPeople would add is the register image itself.

The search page opens with no login and accepts a POST, and then returns the results-page furniture with NO RESULT ROWS for every query. Control: SMITH BIRTHS IN BRISTOL IN 1840 returns zero, which is impossible, and so does Wakefield — a birth this archive already holds from the GRO index at vol 11 p.183. Nothing was searched. Every zero taken from it here is meaningless.

rows.where: the Hornby claim and the Keele graft
rows.note: “You are not allowed to search for posts in this forum. Please login below or register.” Searching needs an account, let alone posting. No account was created. Putting the Hornby evidence to the forum is a job for a person with a login, and is now an errand.

rows.holds: 26 records in Italy, Marriages 1809-1900, with both spouses named
rows.note: Readable WITHOUT signing in, and no bot check appeared. Falco brides and grooms at Arienzo with their spouses — Loffredo, Abatiello, Di Lucia, Librera, Perrotta — and FALCO GIOVANNA married to CRISCI ANIELLO, Crisci being one of the Falco archive's own surnames. This is that archive's ground; the coverage is recorded here, not the records.

The category filter mangles to `life-events-bmds` in the URL and the search then returns zero whatever else is asked, while the same query without it returns results. The third broken FindMyPast parameter found in two days, after yearofbirth+keywordsplace on the census and the Find a Grave locationId.
